```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
# Counts quoted in the prose are read from the register, never typed: this
# article once said two claims were failing after one had been fixed. The
# source register is used when the article is built from the source tree, so a
# register edited without regenerating inst/claims.yml cannot publish stale
# verdicts; otherwise the installed copy.
claims <- fleetcheck::read_claims(if (file.exists("../claims.yml")) "../claims.yml" else
  system.file("claims.yml", package = "fleetcheck"))
n_fail <- sum(claims$status == "fail")
n_band <- sum(grepl("replicate band", claims$criterion, fixed = TRUE))
eng <- function(n) if (n <= 10) c("no", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six",
                                  "seven", "eight", "nine", "ten")[n + 1L] else format(n)
```

## Claims and criteria

The unit of evidence is a claim, not a scenario. Each claim has a criterion that
decides it and a verdict, so the result is a decision rather than a number to
interpret. A claim can fail, and `r eng(n_fail)` currently
`r if (n_fail == 1) "does" else "do"`.

Criteria are drawn from the mechanism rather than from the result: "inside the
IBM replicate band", because that band is the noise floor a deterministic model
should land inside, not "at five of six EIRs", because five is what came out.
The replicate band is the IBM median plus or minus 1.28 standard deviations
across replicates, the 10-90% interval of a normal distribution. It adapts as
the comparison gets harder: splitting the IBM by age thins its counts and widens
its spread, so the test becomes more forgiving where the reference is less
certain, and the measured value records this rather than hiding it.

Claims about how a burden is distributed by age are scored only on the age bands
carrying at least 5% of it. The notes on those claims say what the exclusion
costs.

## Statistics

Every comparison statistic is defined once, in `R/metrics.R`, and unit-tested.
`agreement()` returns correlation, RMSE, bias, relative bias and slope together,
because a slope of 1 with a positive bias is a constant offset while a slope
above 1 with no bias is a fan, and either statistic alone hides which.
`replicate_band()` defines the band named in the criteria of `r eng(n_band)`
claims; `band_summary()` scores a set of cells against it, and
`outside_rates()` sets the bar for claims tested over many cells.

Because figures and tables use the same functions, they cannot disagree: the
site-file correlation in `render.R`'s figure and in `tables.R`'s table both come
from `agreement()`.

## Provenance and precision

`stamp()` records, with every result, the `fleet` and `malariasimulation`
versions and the commits they were installed from, the R version, the platform,
the date, and any fields the run adds. A package installed from a local source
tree has no commit to record, so that field is `null`; `fleet`'s `Built` field
is recorded beside it to show when and on what it was built.

The site-file statistics also record the age grid and the mosquito sub-step
count they were measured at. Their snapshot carries two stamps, which are not
interchangeable. `run` records the site-file sweep, including the `fleet`
version that produced the per-country results, and changes only when the sweep
is repeated. `summarised` records the pass that reduces those results to the
four numbers on this site; it takes seconds and can be repeated at any later
version. A single stamp would report today's `fleet` against numbers from months
earlier.

Simulation output is quoted to three or four significant figures. `run.R`
rounds the stored summaries to six with `round_sig()` as it writes them, so a
re-run cannot store full precision again. One file keeps full precision:
`rep_eq.csv`, which the drift check in `assess.R` compares against at a
tolerance of 1e-6.

## Tiers

Each claim records a tier: the cost of reproducing it.

| Tier | Cost | Who can reproduce it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | seconds | anyone, from the committed summaries |
| 1 | minutes | anyone; re-runs `fleet` only |
| 2 | about 2 hours | anyone with about 10 cores |
| 3 | about 30 minutes | anyone with 4 cores and the site files, which are not redistributable |

These costs are for *P. falciparum*. For *P. vivax*, tier 1 takes a few minutes
and tier 2 about an hour.

Tier 3 is the 63-country site-file comparison. Its figures and statistics are
public, but the site files behind them are not redistributable, so nobody
outside the project can repeat it: a limitation of the evidence, not a property
of the result. The constraint is the inputs rather than the
compute: the sweep re-runs `fleet` only, because the IBM arm is the pre-run
diagnostic shipped with each site file.

## Reproducing the results

Installation, the tier-0 checks and the `fleet`-only drift check are in the
[README](../index.html#installation). Paths below are relative to the repository
root. No script has a hardcoded path: each finds the checkout by walking up to
`DESCRIPTION`, so it runs from any working directory.

`R/` holds the unit-tested package code listed in the
[reference](../reference/index.html). `validations/` has one directory per body
of evidence, with its scripts and committed results; `01-seed-stability` to
`04-parameter-draws` each have a README with script-level detail. Raw model
output is never committed, only summaries and their stamps.

### Scenario comparison

`validations/02-scenarios/` runs every scenario through both models on the same
parameter list. Its `assess.R` re-runs `fleet` alone against the committed IBM
rows, which stay valid for any change to `fleet` because the IBM does not depend
on it. It reports two things separately: whether anything moved (`fleet` now
against `fleet`'s committed rows), and whether the match still holds (`fleet`
against the IBM medians and replicate bands, at the thresholds the claims rest
on). Only the second fails the run by default, with exit status 1, so the script
can gate CI.

```bash
CMP_ONLY=eir_20,smc Rscript validations/02-scenarios/assess.R   # a subset, seconds
CMP_STRICT=1 Rscript validations/02-scenarios/assess.R          # also fail if any number moved
```

Before re-running both models, run the smoke path. It runs every scenario end to
end at a 4-year horizon with one replicate, in about two minutes, and writes to
`validations/02-scenarios/results/smoke/`, so it cannot touch the committed
results.

```bash
CMP_SMOKE=1 Rscript validations/02-scenarios/run.R
```

The full run takes about two hours on ten cores. It runs the IBM `N_REP` times
per scenario on a PSOCK cluster of ten workers (fewer with `CMP_WORKERS`) and
re-stamps `ibm_reference.json`. After a change to `fleet` alone,
`CMP_FLEET_ONLY=1` refreshes `fleet`'s rows in minutes and keeps the IBM's.

```bash
Rscript validations/02-scenarios/run.R
CMP_FLEET_ONLY=1 Rscript validations/02-scenarios/run.R
```

The *P. vivax* suite is the same scripts under `CMP_PARASITE=pv`, with results in
`validations/02-scenarios/results/pv/`. It runs on its own transmission grid
(EIR 0.3 to 30, against 1 to 120 for falciparum), without SMC, PMC or RTS,S,
and with radical cure in their place: `malariasimulation` cannot run
chemoprevention under vivax, and its vaccines carry no vivax calibration.

```bash
CMP_PARASITE=pv Rscript validations/02-scenarios/run.R
CMP_PARASITE=pv CMP_FLEET_ONLY=1 Rscript validations/02-scenarios/run.R
CMP_PARASITE=pv Rscript validations/02-scenarios/assess.R
```

The `speed` and `speed-pv` tables time both models side by side, one run of
each, alone on one core. Run them on an otherwise idle machine:

```bash
Rscript validations/02-scenarios/speed.R                   # about 15 min: results/speed.csv, vignettes/tab_speed.md
CMP_PARASITE=pv Rscript validations/02-scenarios/speed.R   # about 25 min: results/pv/speed.csv, vignettes/tab_speed_pv.md
```

The figures and tables are redrawn from the committed results in seconds,
without running a model:

```bash
Rscript validations/02-scenarios/render.R      # cmp_*.png into man/figures/ and vignettes/
Rscript validations/02-scenarios/tables.R      # validations/02-scenarios/results/tables.md
Rscript validations/02-scenarios/render_pv.R   # the vivax figures, cmp_pv_*.png
Rscript validations/02-scenarios/tables_pv.R   # validations/02-scenarios/results/pv/tables.md
```

Neither pair redraws its site-file panel, which is a snapshot of tier-3 results
that cannot be repeated without the site files. `CMP_REFRESH_SITES=1` re-takes
the snapshot from the tier-3 results in
`validations/03-real-settings/results/raw/`.

### Seed stability and parameter draws

`validations/01-seed-stability/run.R` reproduces `seed-stability` and
`seed-stability-pv` in a few minutes, running `fleet` only, and writes
`results/seed_stability.json` and `results/seed_stability_pv.json`.

`validations/04-parameter-draws/` is also tier 2: eight of
`set_parameter_draw()`'s posterior draws at three EIRs, for `parameter-draws`.
`select.R` chooses the draws. `run.R` runs both models, in about two hours on
four workers; `assess.R` re-runs `fleet` alone against the committed IBM rows;
`render.R` draws the figure. `diagnose.R` tests what moves the severe-incidence
gap, with 40 IBM runs in about fifteen minutes.

```bash
Rscript validations/01-seed-stability/run.R
Rscript validations/04-parameter-draws/run.R
Rscript validations/04-parameter-draws/assess.R
Rscript validations/04-parameter-draws/render.R
Rscript validations/04-parameter-draws/diagnose.R
```

### Site-file comparison

Tier 3 runs from this repository given the malariaverse site files, located by
`FLEET_VALIDATE`:

```bash
FLEET_VALIDATE=/path/to/site-files Rscript validations/03-real-settings/run.R
Rscript validations/03-real-settings/assess.R
```

The *P. vivax* arm is the same pair under `CMP_PARASITE=pv`, with results in
`validations/03-real-settings/results/pv/`. A vivax run of `fleet` costs about
thirteen times a falciparum one, so each country is represented by at most ten
sub-sites, spread evenly across its vivax EIR range. `diagnose.R` draws every
sub-site's monthly clinical series, IBM against `fleet`, as a PDF for
investigating where they disagree; its output is not committed.

With a single site file, `example-one-site.R` runs the same pipeline on one
sub-site in about two minutes: it subsets the site file, converts ITN usage to
a distribution, builds the parameter list, seeds both models from it, reduces
both through `postie`, and scores them with the same `agreement()` the register
uses. One sub-site against one IBM replicate shows that the pipeline runs; it is
not evidence about the model, so read the shape of the output rather than its
third decimal. `validations/03-real-settings/README.md` describes each step and
the details that matter.

```bash
FLEET_VALIDATE=/path/to/fleet_validate Rscript validations/03-real-settings/example-one-site.R BFA
```

### Updating the register

Edit `claims.yml` (the criterion, the measured value, the verdict), then
regenerate its rendered copies:

```bash
Rscript report/make_scoreboard.R
```

This rewrites the register list and badges in `README.md`, `pkgdown/index.md`
(generated from `README.md`) and `inst/claims.yml`. Do not edit those copies by
hand: CI runs the same script with `--check` and fails if they do not match.
The evidence articles read `claims.yml` when the site is built:

```bash
Rscript -e 'pkgdown::build_site()'
```

### Environment variables

| Variable | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `CMP_PARASITE=pv` | run the *P. vivax* suite, or the vivax arm of tier 3, instead of *P. falciparum* |
| `CMP_SMOKE=1` | 4-year, one-replicate end-to-end check, written to `results/smoke/` |
| `CMP_ONLY=a,b` | run or check only these scenarios (countries in tier 3), merging into the existing results |
| `CMP_FLEET_ONLY=1` | re-run `fleet`'s rows only, keeping the committed IBM rows |
| `CMP_STRICT=1` | make `assess.R` fail on any movement, not only on lost agreement |
| `CMP_WORKERS` | worker pool size for `run.R` (default 10 in `02-scenarios`, 4 in `04-parameter-draws`) |
| `CMP_REFRESH_SITES=1` | re-take the site-file snapshot behind the tier-3 figure panels and tables |
| `FLEET_VALIDATE` | location of the site files; required by the tier-3 sweep, and `../fleet_validate`, beside the checkout, by default elsewhere |
| `FLEET_LIB` | library path prepended to `.libPaths()`, for installations that do not pick up `R_LIBS_USER` |
| `FLEETCHECK_ROOT` | the checkout root, for a job that runs from outside it |
